summary: A deployed default Flask histogram turned request-controlled raw paths into unbounded labels: at every checkpoint Flask series equaled 17 times the method/path/status tuple count plus 13, and 2,476 new tuples produced exactly all 42,092 new Flask series. Confirmed automated-style 404 probing triggered expensive multiprocess collection and serialization, and Kubernetes OOM-killed the sole relay.
impact: Production was intermittently unavailable during an approximately 87-minute crash loop, and repeated termination created an unquantified risk of losing active memory-backed relay state; no customer data loss was proven.
fix: Status is operationally Resolved as of 2026-09-05T19:53:19Z. Production Helm revision 7 runs ghcr.io/futuroptimist/tokenplace-relay:sha-6c39adc (OCI index sha256:543fde33aff45253630090b52d16163e3586da12c973f5c4a658ddc8927d0a68; source 6c39adc64e7bed4f85d07164aa2860e637919ca9; public version 0.1.1). Authenticated scraping was restored: the final payload was 35,751 bytes and 227 samples with zero unmatched-path canary and pid-label occurrences; Prometheus observed six successful up samples, min_over_time(up)=1, scrape duration 0.011584181 seconds, and tokenplace_instrumentation_up=1. During the six-minute soak memory stayed between 65,101,824 and 65,425,408 bytes of 268,435,456, compute polls rose from 222 to 260, and restarts, HTTP 429, and HTTP 5xx remained zero. No intentionally disabled monitoring functionality remains.
lessons: The exact 17-times series fingerprint and low-reuse 404 aggregates confirmed both the cardinality defect and automated-style trigger without actor attribution. Release parity and negative-test coverage must prevent divergent artifacts from omitting existing hardening; pod-lifetime multiprocess state needs safe startup cleanup, and one replica amplified the outcome. Operational resolution is separate from preventive-work completion, so all linked action-item issues remain open pending independent implementation and verification.
